title: Adaptive backoff and stale-segment compaction for interrupted generations
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect or experience long pauses during streaming generations (especially around function/tool calls and structured outputs), server-side in-flight segments, KV cache slices, and ephemeral checkpoints linger and increase memory/IO pressure. Current behavior either retains too much state (wasting resources) or aggressively discards prefixes (hurting resume accuracy).

Goal: Implement an adaptive backoff + stale-segment compaction strategy that: (1) applies a tiered grace window based on request-age, client reconnect heuristics, and model QoS; (2) compacts leftover partial segments into compact checkpoint artifacts that are cheaper to retain; and (3) exposes a resumable token and a best-effort prefix snapshot for clients that reconnect within the grace window.

Non‑goals: This ticket does not change the public streaming protocol or SDK APIs. It focuses on server-side lifecycle and resource management for interrupted/incomplete generations. Resume semantics will remain best-effort (no strict delivery guarantees for partially-sent deltas).
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive tenure configured: short (10s), medium (60s), long (15m) grace windows that can be tuned per-customer/route.
When a client disconnects, server creates a compact checkpoint after the short grace window and frees hot KV slices; compact checkpoint can be rehydrated for resume within medium window.
Compaction reduces memory footprint of retained interrupted generations by >= 4x in the benchmarked chat workloads (seq_len 512, beamless sampling).
Metrics: new telemetry for 'stale_segment_compact_count', 'resume_success_rate', and 'post_disconnect_memory_delta' are emitted and surfaced in Console per-route dashboard.

Integration: function/toolcall boundaries are preserved in compact checkpoints so resumed generations do not re-invoke idempotent external tools; documented caveats added to Console's troubleshooting guide.
E2E tests: simulated abrupt TCP socket close and SDK-level reconnect validate resume token acceptance and graceful fallback to fresh generation when checkpoint absent or expired.

notes: Implementation details: use a two-phase cleanup: first convert to compact checkpoint (protobuf with compressed tokenized prefix + functioncall tombstones + minimal KV references), then schedule async compaction-to-archival after medium window. Grace windows default can be overridden by customer route config and tuned by runtime heuristics (e.g., request QPS, model latency). Avoid exposing internals in API; resume token opaque to clients. Ensure compaction job respects tenant isolation and backpressure so it doesn't contend with hot inference workloads.
